Hollywood is increasingly viewing YouTube as a major competitor, and according to a new report, free tiers from streaming platforms like Disney+ and Paramount+ may be the answer.

Streaming platforms like Disney+, Paramount+, and Netflix are exploring free tiers in different ways

Reportedly, Disney's Head of Product and Technology, Adam Smith, earlier mentioned "the possibility of offering free content" during an internal streaming platform meeting.

These measures aim to remove the barriers posed by Disney+'s paywall in order to expand reach. This way, Disney can more easily sell paid subscriptions to users who are already accustomed to using the app.

Paramount reportedly has a similar idea: "According to an internal briefing obtained by Business Insider, Paramount's flagship streaming platform plans to expand the movies and shows available to non-subscribers."

Netflix's remarks about launching a free service are mainly directed at markets outside the US, but depending on how free tiers from other streaming platforms perform, the situation could change at any time.

Part of the push for each streaming platform comes from YouTube's continuously growing user engagement and market share. Disney+ had previously planned to add free, YouTube-like user-generated content, but with the Sora project falling through and the breakdown of Disney's partnership with OpenAI, the prospects for these plans have become uncertain.

What do you think about streaming platforms rolling out more free streaming options? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
